dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Arkhium really has incredible research potential. I have to find a way to get in and take a look...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Whatever you do, you're not allowed to research Arkhium!

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Ugh, why are you here? Don't you understand? That explosion before was just an accident. Arkhium still has plenty of potential as a subject of research.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: And such incidents are inevitable during research. You lose a few researchers? Hire a few more. You destroy a lab? Build another. As long as the supply of Arkhium is guaranteed, I can get the research project up and running again.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: ...Why are you looking at me like that? Did I say something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Hmm... How can I get in?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was your research that caused this tragedy.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Indeed, it was a tragedy. However, they sacrificed themselves for science, and I salute them.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: But I must insist that you stop trying to pin that explosion on me. I've said it before, and I'll say it again: I wasn't in the Central Laboratory at the time. I was out inspecting other departments.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Some knucklehead must have spilled a cup of coffee, or accidentally pulled the wrong lever. Who knows how those idiots screwed up? At any rate, they ruined my lab and the entire Arkhium project!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about Loillier and Concini?

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Financial backers for my research, that's all. They only cared about making Mora. They didn't understand the first thing about technology, and couldn't even handle simple tasks like procuring precision instruments.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: I'd had enough. I was forced to assemble the instruments myself and rebuild the entire lab.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: They ended up being more interested in Nacker's shoddy prototype, and they kicked me out of the lab!

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: They asked me to work on peripheral suppressors instead. How absurd!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're the project leader. Don't try to evade responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Ha! So you came all this way just to lecture me?

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: I never asked to be the project leader. If the Institute hadn't imposed a deadline on my research—

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: I wouldn't have had to hire that gaggle of fools to assist me. If I had the time to personally oversee every project, that accident would never have happened!

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Forget it. I won't waste any more of my time explaining it to you. When I get out of the Fortress of Meropide, I must get it through to the Institute to restart the research.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What carrot did they dangle in front of you?

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Mora, fame, mansions, the whole nine yards. But I'm not interested in any of that.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Mora won't necessarily buy you any raw Arkhium, and fame won't attract top research assistants.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: As for the mansions... maybe I'd consider it if they were filled with precision instruments, but that clearly wouldn't be the case.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: I had no place to restart my research at the time, so I had to agree to rebuild the lab there.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: And now, thanks to Nacker, I don't even have my lab anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will the Fontaine Research Institute take you back?

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: If I were Raimondo, I wouldn't let Edwin Eastinghouse himself be idle and outside the Institute.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Otherwise... Hmph! Does he really want the Institute to turn into a Fonta development factory?

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: But now that that Choiseul has moved his office into the Institute... He might try to stop me from returning...

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: I just want to conduct my own research in peace. Is that too much to ask?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Whatever you do, you're not allowed to research Arkhium!

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Ugh, why are you here? Don't you understand? That explosion before was just an accident. Arkhium still has plenty of potential as a subject of research.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: And such incidents are inevitable during research. You lose a few researchers? Hire a few more. You destroy a lab? Build another. As long as the supply of Arkhium is guaranteed, I can get the research project up and running again.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: What are you looking at me like that for? Am I wrong? I know you saw that ship Jurieu built, the Wingalet or whatever.

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Jurieu, Jurieu... And what energy source could he have used, if not Arkhium? That ship alone proves the value of the stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Edwin Eastinghouse
dialogues.text: Although if you ask me, that tub of his was underpowered. There's room for improvement in his catalytic processes... yes, that's right! The tech I already developed should have been used...
